notes.title: Polysomnography Report
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 09/17/2025
Patient: Valentine Altenwerth, 86-year-old male

Diagnostic in-laboratory polysomnography performed 09/17/2025. Total apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 29.8 events/hour. Central and mixed apneas comprised 4% of all events. The study showed intermittent oxygen desaturations corresponding with respiratory events. Sleep stages were fragmented with decreased REM sleep duration.

Impression: Moderate severity sleep apnea with predominantly obstructive events. Treatment with positive airway pressure therapy is recommended. Follow-up in sleep clinic is advised for therapy titration and monitoring.

Sleep Medicine Consultation Note
Date: 08/22/2026
Patient: Valentine Altenwerth, 87-year-old male

Reason for Consultation:
Evaluation and management of sleep-disordered breathing.

History:
Mr. Altenwerth is an 87-year-old male referred for assessment of sleep apnea management. He has a history of obstructive sleep apnea diagnosed several years ago.

Physical Examination:
BMI 33.9 kg/m2.

Sleep Study and Treatment:
CPAP intolerance: download shows average use 3.0 hours per night on 27% of nights despite mask refitting; shared decision-making with the patient documented that CPAP is not tolerated.

Plan:
Discuss alternative therapies for sleep apnea management including oral appliance therapy and positional therapy. Recommend follow-up sleep study to assess current severity. Continue monitoring symptoms and oxygenation.

Summary:
Mr. Altenwerth has significant CPAP intolerance despite efforts to optimize mask fit and usage. Alternative treatment options will be explored to improve his sleep quality and reduce apnea events.

Otolaryngology Consultation Note
Date: 09/27/2026
Patient: Valentine Altenwerth, 87-year-old male

Reason for Consultation:
87-year-old man referred for hypoglossal nerve stimulation evaluation.

History:
History of myasthenia gravis with bulbar weakness.

Examination:
Oropharynx: tonsils size 1, no other anatomic obstruction.

Procedures:
Drug-induced sleep endoscopy 09/19/2026: anteroposterior collapse at the velum without complete concentric collapse.

Assessment and Plan:
The patient demonstrates anteroposterior collapse at the velum on sleep endoscopy, without complete concentric collapse. Tonsillar size is minimal, and no other anatomic obstructions are noted. Given the history of myasthenia gravis with bulbar weakness, careful consideration is warranted for hypoglossal nerve stimulation therapy. Further multidisciplinary evaluation will be pursued to optimize management.
